Query: we are a 50-person SaaS company with many women employees, we collect user data and bill overseas clients — what are all our compliance obligations
Valid as of: 2026-10-15

SUMMARY
- Corporate Governance: Corporate governance for a 50-person startup involves maintaining a board of directors, ensuring financial transparency with shareholders, and formalizing board reporting.
- Corporate Governance (not addressed by retrieved provisions): The provided provisions do not contain specific corporate governance obligations triggered by having exactly 50 employees.
- Data Protection: SaaS companies must obtain clear, informed consent, provide transparent privacy notices, and implement robust security and grievance redressal mechanisms.
- Data Protection: Significant Data Fiduciaries face additional requirements including mandatory audits, impact assessments, and potential data localization.
- Data Protection: some of these obligations are not yet in force on 2026-10-15; each step below shows the date it applies from.
- Data Protection (not addressed by retrieved provisions): Specific compliance obligations for different company sizes (other than the 'Significant Data Fiduciary' classification) or specific employee types are not detailed beyond general employment-related processing.
- Intellectual Property: SaaS companies must ensure copyright ownership of software through written contracts and can protect brand usage by registering licensees as 'registered users'.
- Intellectual Property: Copyright for software is protected as a literary work, granting exclusive rights to reproduce, adapt, and commercially rent the code.
- Intellectual Property (not addressed by retrieved provisions): Specific compliance requirements for independent contractors (as opposed to employees under a contract of service) and specific procedures for international trademark protection.
- Taxation & GST: SaaS companies exporting services can treat them as zero-rated supplies, allowing for refunds of unutilised input tax credit or exports without payment of integrated tax under bond/LUT.
- Taxation & GST: The place of supply for online information and database access or retrieval services is the location of the recipient.
- Taxation & GST (not addressed by retrieved provisions): Specific tax rates, filing deadlines for GSTR forms, and detailed income tax computation procedures for SaaS companies beyond the general definition of export turnover.
- Employment & Workplace: Employers must ensure equal pay and non-discrimination, provide maternity benefits, prevent sexual harassment, and constitute an Internal Complaints Committee.
- Employment & Workplace: Women may work night shifts with consent and safety safeguards, and must be searched only by women if searches are conducted.
- Employment & Workplace (not addressed by retrieved provisions): The provided provisions do not contain specific compliance obligations triggered by the '50-person' company size threshold.

ACTION CHECKLIST
**Corporate Governance**
Step 1: Ensure the company has at least two directors, including at least one director who has stayed in India for 182+ days during the financial year. — [ca_2013_sec_149] (applies to: private) [NOTE: only partly supported by the cited text]
Step 2: Approve financial statements by the Board of Directors and attach a Board's Report including a Directors' Responsibility Statement, details on fraud, loans, and related-party transactions. — [ca_2013_sec_134] (applies to: private) [NOTE: only partly supported by the cited text]
Step 3: Send audited financial statements and the Board's report to all members at least 21 days before the annual general meeting. — [ca_2013_sec_136] (applies to: private)
Step 4: Authorize a representative via board resolution if a corporate entity (such as a VC fund) is a member of the company, allowing them to attend and vote at meetings. — [ca_2013_sec_113] (applies to: private)

**Data Protection**
Step 5: Provide a clear, standalone notice in English or any Eighth Schedule language detailing the personal data collected, the purpose of processing, and how to exercise rights or file complaints. — [dpdp_act_2023_sec_5] (applies to: both) [NOTE: Not yet in force on 2026-10-15; applies from 2027-05-13.]
Step 6: Ensure consent is free, specific, informed, and unambiguous; provide an easy mechanism for users to withdraw consent. — [dpdp_act_2023_sec_6] (applies to: both) [NOTE: Not yet in force on 2026-10-15; applies from 2027-05-13.]
Step 7: Process data only for specified purposes, medical emergencies, or employment-related needs, unless consent is withdrawn. — [dpdp_act_2023_sec_7] (applies to: both) [NOTE: Not yet in force on 2026-10-15; applies from 2027-05-13.]
Step 8: Implement reasonable security safeguards, use valid contracts for third-party processors, report data breaches to the Board and affected users, and maintain a grievance redressal mechanism. — [dpdp_act_2023_sec_8] (applies to: both) [NOTE: Not yet in force on 2026-10-15; applies from 2027-05-13.]
Step 9: Erase personal data upon withdrawal of consent or when the specified purpose is no longer served, unless retention is required by law. — [dpdp_act_2023_sec_8] (applies to: both) [NOTE: Not yet in force on 2026-10-15; applies from 2027-05-13.]
Step 10: Obtain verifiable parental consent before processing data of children and refrain from tracking, behavioral monitoring, or targeted advertising directed at children. — [dpdp_act_2023_sec_9] (applies to: both) [NOTE: Not yet in force on 2026-10-15; applies from 2027-05-13.]
Step 11: If classified as a Significant Data Fiduciary, appoint an India-based Data Protection Officer, conduct periodic Data Protection Impact Assessments, and hire an independent data auditor. — [dpdp_act_2023_sec_10] (applies to: both) [NOTE: Not yet in force on 2026-10-15; applies from 2027-05-13.]
Step 12: Ensure privacy notices are standalone, itemized, and include a link for easy consent withdrawal. — [dpdp_rules_2025_sec_3] (applies to: both) [NOTE: Not yet in force on 2026-10-15; applies from 2027-05-13.]
Step 13: If a Significant Data Fiduciary, perform algorithmic due diligence, report audit findings to the Board, and comply with specific data localization requirements if mandated by the Central Government. — [dpdp_rules_2025_sec_13] (applies to: both) [NOTE: Not yet in force on 2026-10-15; applies from 2027-05-13.]
Step 14: Avoid unauthorized disclosure of personal information obtained under contract to prevent personal liability for wrongful loss or gain. — [information_technology_act_2000_sec_72A] (applies to: both)

**Intellectual Property**
Step 15: Ensure all copyright assignments are in writing and signed, as they are otherwise invalid. — [copyright_act_1957_sec_19]
Step 16: Specify the duration and territorial extent in copyright assignment contracts; otherwise, they default to five years and India-only coverage. — [copyright_act_1957_sec_19]
Step 17: Recognize that the company is the first owner of copyright for software created by employees under a contract of service, unless an agreement states otherwise. — [copyright_act_1957_sec_17]
Step 18: Register licensees (resellers, subsidiaries, or franchisees) as 'registered users' to ensure their use of the trademark counts as use by the proprietor and prevents non-use cancellation. — [trademarks_act_1999_sec_48] [NOTE: only partly supported by the cited text]
Step 19: Apply in writing to the Registrar to register trademarks, noting that multi-class applications are permitted for different goods and services. — [trademarks_act_1999_sec_18]

**Taxation & GST**
Step 20: Determine the place of supply for online information and database access or retrieval services as the location of the recipient, based on specific conditions regarding address, payment method, and internet connectivity. — [igst_act_2017_sec_13]
Step 21: Classify the export of services as a zero-rated supply, which allows for the availing of input tax credit. — [igst_act_2017_sec_16]
Step 22: If making zero-rated supplies without payment of integrated tax, furnish a bond or Letter of Undertaking (LUT) in FORM GST RFD-11 prior to export. — [cgst_rules_2017_rule_96a] (applies to: private)
Step 23: Ensure receipt of payment for services in convertible foreign exchange within one year of the invoice date to maintain the validity of the export under bond/LUT. — [cgst_rules_2017_rule_96a] (applies to: private) [NOTE: only partly supported by the cited text]
Step 24: Claim a refund of unutilised input tax credit for zero-rated supplies made without payment of tax, subject to providing necessary documentary evidence. — [cgst_act_2017_sec_54] [NOTE: only partly supported by the cited text]

**Employment & Workplace**
Step 25: Ensure equal remuneration for men and women for the same or similar work; pay rates must be leveled up to the higher rate, not reduced. — [era_1976_sec_4]
Step 26: Prohibit discrimination against women in recruitment, promotion, training, and transfer, except where legally restricted. — [era_1976_sec_5]
Step 27: Provide maternity benefits (paid leave) for up to 26 weeks (or 12 weeks for those with two or more surviving children) to eligible women who have worked for at least 80 days in the preceding 12 months. — [mba_1961_sec_5] [NOTE: only partly supported by the cited text]
Step 28: Provide maternity benefits to women whose wages exceed the ESI wage ceiling, provided they meet the 80-day work requirement. — [mba_1961_sec_5B] [NOTE: only partly supported by the cited text]
Step 29: Prohibit sexual harassment at the workplace, including conduct that creates a hostile environment or involves threats/promises regarding employment status. — [posh_2013_sec_3]
Step 30: Constitute an Internal Complaints Committee at each office or administrative unit via written order, ensuring at least half the members are women and including an external NGO member. — [posh_2013_sec_4]
Step 31: Permit women to work night shifts (before 6 a.m. and beyond 7 p.m.) only with their consent and subject to safety and working-hour conditions. — [oshwc_2020_sec_43]
Step 32: Ensure that if women employees are subject to searches at entry/exit points, they are searched only by women. — [ieso_rules_1946_IA_21]
